standard_prerequisites: The algebraic closure is algebraically closed: every element has a p-th root
Freshman's dream exponent law in characteristic p: (alpha - beta)^p = alpha^p - beta^p, so equal p-th powers differ by a p-th power of an element of the field, which is zero only for zero
core_obligations: alpha is a root of P(x^p) exactly when alpha^p is a root of P, so the roots of P(x^p) are the p-th roots of the roots of P

The p-th power map on the algebraic closure is bijective: surjective since the closure is algebraically closed, injective since alpha^p = beta^p gives (alpha - beta)^p = 0 in characteristic p and hence alpha = beta
A bijection of the ambient field restricts to a bijection between the two root sets, so they have the same cardinality not counting multiplicity
proof_roadmap: Relate the two root sets through the p-th power map
Prove the p-th power map is bijective on the algebraic closure
